name: Index of Industrial Production - General Index
remarks: Lag placeholder - verify against release calendar. MoSPI-downloaded files only cover 26-54% of expected months per base (a filter applied before download, not a parser defect). Gaps in the 1993-94, 2004-05, and 2011-12 bases were backfilled ONCE from an RBI DBIE export ("Index of Industrial Production.xlsx", General Index) via corrections.csv -- see the 2026-08-27 entries there, reason field cites the source. That file is intentionally not wired in as a live `bases:` source: MoSPI remains the source of truth going forward, this was a one-time gap-fill only. The 2022-23 base switched to "iip_general/iip_55.xlsx" (MoSPI eSankhyiki long-format export, `mospi_iip_long`), which is complete for the months it covers (39/39, 2023-04 to 2026-06) and agrees exactly with the old file on every overlapping month -- a genuine MoSPI replacement, not a one-off. Also note: for the 1993-94 base, 31 months where MoSPI and the RBI export overlap actually disagree (MoSPI consistently higher, up to +17.6, concentrated in Jan-Jun 2005-2009) -- those were NOT touched, left on the original MoSPI value; worth a manual look if that period matters for the model.

name: Merchandise Trade Export to Import Ratio
remarks: Switched from FRED's XTEITT01INM156S (an OECD MEI relay, frozen since Nov 2023) to a value computed directly from India's own Ministry of Commerce/DGCI&S trade statistics -- the same file already used for non_oil_non_gold_imports, and current through the latest release rather than stale. India's own trade classification doesn't exactly match OECD's methodology, so the ratio for a given month differs by several points from the old FRED-derived value (e.g. ~62% vs ~66% for Nov 2023) -- a genuine methodology difference, not a bug, and switching sources introduces a one-time level discontinuity in the stored history at the switchover date. Lag placeholder.

name: Euro Area Industrial Production
remarks: Switched from FRED's PRINTO01EZQ661S (an OECD-relayed QUARTERLY series, frozen since Q3 2023) to Eurostat's own primary dataset sts_inpr_m (EA20, seasonally/calendar adjusted, 2021=100), pulled directly from Eurostat's open JSON API (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/sts_inpr_m, no key required) on 2026-09-16. This is genuinely primary (Eurostat is the originating EU statistical agency), MONTHLY rather than quarterly (a real upgrade for nowcasting timeliness), and current through the latest release rather than stale by nearly 3 years. The last few months in any future refresh may carry Eurostat's own "provisional" flag; treat as normal revision-prone data, same as WPI's own most-recent-months caveat elsewhere in this file. Lag placeholder - verify against Eurostat's own release calendar.
